control: Access needs a permitted role, membership of the matter, and a role valid for the matter's profile
Every matter record is stored and queried under its matter id; a record cannot be read or rewritten across matters
Legal sources are reachable only if registered, approved with licence and status semantics recorded, and listed on the matter
Outbound network is refused by default; a window opens for one approved host at a time
Originals are stored once, read-only and hash-addressed; every finding is re-checked against unchanged source text
Every document is accounted for: read, or the gap explicitly accepted by a named person
Document and source text is fenced as untrusted data; text addressed to a model is flagged, held, and kept out of every model prompt
Each cited authority is looked up in the approved sources; a citation absent from a source that is complete for its kind fails
Whether an authority is still good law is checked separately from whoever cited it, for the relevant date, with a freshness limit
evidence: current_law verification results; source version ids

control: A proposition is verified only if it is the source's own words or a named person confirms it; two models agreeing is not verification
A finding is verified only when every check its kind requires has passed; a held finding holds everything relying on it
A hold closes only when its checks pass or a named, authorised person excludes or waives with reasons; an override needs a separate permission
No output states a decision; for decision-makers and neutrals none says who should succeed; drafted arguments add no figure or citation of their own
Reliance requires approval by a named human reviewer on the matter, with every stated limit acknowledged; an agent can hold no role
Approval is bound to the exact report reviewed: the hash must match, the file must be unaltered, and the findings must not have changed
Audit events are chained with HMAC-SHA-256; no key means no governed run; edits, removals and truncation are detected
For each run the store is reconciled with the ledger: every step, hold, review and the verification set must have a matching event
The ledger refuses content-bearing fields and long strings, so it holds identifiers and hashes rather than document text

A run can be stopped at any moment: the step at work ends at its next model answer, document or issue, no later step starts, and nothing a step saves afterwards undoes the stop; it restarts only on a named, authorised decision with a reason, and re-running reproduces the same findings; a report returned for correction restarts from the beginning unless a person chooses a step, and a restart that would not read a document added since the papers were read is refused
Only an approved report can be released, only to entitled recipients confirmed by a named person, and it is staged rather than sent
Incident-grade holds open an incident automatically; incidents close only with containment and reasons recorded
Monitoring is computed from control evidence: failed checks, overrides, unchallenged approvals, open incidents, version changes
Closing a matter ends access and can delete documents, text and indexes while keeping the decision record and the ledger
A policy file can tighten behaviour but cannot switch off human release, fail-closed audit or matter isolation; unlisted actions are refused
Inside ELI v3 the host's other capabilities are refused, no decision is exposed to the assistant, and capability output carries no matter content
Jurisdiction packs hold structure and citation grammar only, ship unvalidated, and the report says so until a qualified lawyer validates them
evidence: pack status in configuration.json; report limits

control: An evidence pack for any run can be exported: manifests, findings, checks, decisions, versions and the audit extract, all hashed
The server accepts only authenticated named users, applies the same service rules as every other front end, and answers no route without credentials except health, boundaries, the page and sign-in

No service acts on a name alone: identity must be established by a front end that checked a credential (passphrase session, passphrase sign-in, or token), and a signed-in person cannot act as anyone else
evidence: sign_in events; access_denied events with reason identity_not_established

control: A decision recorded in a person's name (resolve a hold, verify, review, restart, release, close, approve a source, change the model, manage users) needs that person's passphrase again at the moment of the decision
evidence: auth field of each decision event (…+step-up)

control: Every audit event records how the actor's identity was established, so work done under a test or demonstration harness can never pass as a real sign-in
evidence: auth field on every audit event

control: Matter chat answers only from the matter's documents, findings and approved sources, shows where each passage comes from, marks what may not be relied on, refuses to give the decision, and keeps only model sentences grounded in the sources they cite
evidence: chat_query events (hash of the question, counts)

control: Changing the model is a governed change: it needs its own permission, the verifier must be a different model, a model server off this machine must be an approved host, and the change is recorded

The desktop application is a front end over the same services: it offers only legal and governance functions, shows every refusal in the system's own words, and can do nothing the signed-in person's role cannot

The server listens on this machine only unless told otherwise, refuses to listen beyond it without TLS or a declared trusted proxy, enforces TLS 1.2 as a minimum, and can make a self-signed certificate whose fingerprint it prints

A browser session is an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie (host-bound and Secure over TLS); any change also needs the CSRF value given to the page at sign-in; sessions end when idle or after a fixed time; a session opened by another front end is not accepted

Every request passes one shield before any route: known host name, same-origin for changes, per-client rate budget, declared and bounded body size; every response carries a strict content-security policy and browser protections; no other origin may read a response

Repeated wrong passphrases or codes lock the account for a period on every front end; a locked account is refused even with the right passphrase; only an administrator can unlock it; all of it is recorded
evidence: sign_in audit events with outcome account_locked

control: A second factor (RFC 6238 one-time code) can be set up by any user and is then needed at every sign-in on every front end; a code cannot be used twice; where the server is reachable from other machines it is required before anything else can be reached

The server offers only legal and governance functions; it discloses no server file path, cannot be used to read outside the import area or to call any other machine, never echoes what was sent in a refusal, and its page shows all matter content as text and loads nothing from elsewhere
The whole lifecycle can be carried out through the server by signed-in people alone, with runs executing in the background under the identity of whoever started them
The report marks every authority the system found that no party cited, so that a decision-maker does not rely on it without the parties having been heard on it
evidence: report section 4, column 'Cited by a party'

control: Material filed in confidence by one party, or for the neutral only, is left out of any version built to be shared, and the shared version says how much was withheld

Each matter applies chosen law and standards packages (recommended for its kind and legal system); a run records each package's exact version; the model is told their rules after, never in place of, the system's own; their tightening rules apply; every reviewer confirmation they require must be acknowledged before approval; the report lists every requirement and how it is met
evidence: run framework_versions; report section 9; framework_confirm acknowledgements

control: An organisation's own package cannot be used until a person with the right approves its exact content in their own name; changing it withdraws the approval; text in it that reads as an instruction to an AI system stops it being approved; a run cannot be reported against a package that has changed since

GGUF models run in this process on this machine; they are found in ELI's own model folders; a remote screen chooses one by reference and never sees a path; a configured model that cannot be used is reported and the system runs without it
evidence: configuration_changed audit events with the model fingerprint

control: Opened by ELI v3 as a bundle, ELI Legal keeps its data in its own folder, uses ELI v3's model only through the one inference call the edition allows, and keeps every control it has standalone

A GGUF model is placed on the machine by measurement, not by setting: its costs are read from its own file and the graphics and system memory free when it loads; what llama.cpp itself reports of the load (context, layers on the graphics card, the llama.cpp that ran it) is what is shown and recorded; each step fits its material to the context the model holds and says what it left out, and a reply cut short is refused, not used; the conversation is handed to the model in the form its own chat template takes, the instructions always among it, and any form but plain text is noted on the model's report

The llama.cpp that uses the graphics card is a separate copy, switched on only after it has shown in a process of its own that it can use this machine's card; it comes from this machine (ELI Legal's own folder, the installer, ELI v3's or v2's folder) and is never downloaded; an installed copy uses only one of the built-in version; installing one from a file needs the permission to change the model and is recorded with the file's fingerprint
evidence: configuration_changed audit events (inference_runtime); model_loaded audit events name the llama.cpp in use

control: Each person on a matter has a role on it (lead, decision-maker, case worker, assistant, observer, auditor) that narrows what their account role allows and never widens it; only the lead manages the team; a named reviewer must hold a role that can approve; someone added before matter roles existed keeps exactly what their account allowed
evidence: matter_updated audit events (access_granted, member_role_set); access_denied with reason matter_role_lacks_permission

control: Material is withheld from anyone on a matter whose role does not clear them for it, and from anyone acting for another party when it was given in confidence: in document lists, passages, findings, chat, the report, warnings and the evidence pack; they are told it was withheld and why, never what it says; a drafted argument is never shown more widely than what it rests on; observers and auditors see contact, bank, card and identity numbers masked; oversight of every matter shows none of a matter's content to someone not on it
evidence: content_withheld audit events; evidence pack MANIFEST content and exporter_role_on_matter

control: Every requirement reads as met, met by the software, waiting for the organisation or due for review: what the software does is its controls, and what remains is an organisation action recorded in a named person's name with their passphrase, with its evidence (a form generated from the governance template, a statement, training per person, a registration number, a signed-off document) and a review date

Routine checks run daily and on request: the audit trail, the registers, whether every authority relied on is still good law as a run would judge it today, whether each law package was checked against its official text recently and what in the law calendar has come or is coming into application, the age of source status data, the stored originals, the organisation's compliance work, accounts and training, retention and open work; an authority no longer good law in an approved report and an altered original each open an incident; results about a matter are never shown to someone not on it
evidence: routine_check, incident_opened and law_currency_confirmed audit events

control: Retention periods are set in a named person's name; the audit trail cannot be set below six months and is never truncated; a closed matter's documents, text and indexes are deleted by the routine checks when its period ends, once, with the decision record and ledger kept
evidence: retention_purge audit events; OA-09 compliance record

control: A built-in evaluation prepares a matter with known defects planted in it, in a workspace of its own, and records how many were caught, how many facts were verbatim and how many holds were unexpected, against thresholds the provider declares; falling short leaves the accuracy requirement waiting
evidence: OA-07 compliance record with its measures and thresholds

control: The Annex IV technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity are drafted from the system's own records, mark what only the provider can state, and are signed off by their hash; the declaration says it is not to be issued until the conformity assessment and the actions before real use are recorded
evidence: compliance_document_generated audit events with the document's hash; OA-05 and OA-12 sign-off records

control: A serious incident carries its Art. 73 reporting deadline (15 days; 10 for a death; 2 for a widespread infringement or critical-infrastructure disruption) until a named person decides whether it is reportable and records the report; the routine checks show it as due or overdue; the deadline counts from when the provider or deployer became aware, recorded with how it became known, which may be moved earlier but never later, and from the incident's entry only until awareness is recorded; each serious incident has an owner and a different stand-in who may manage incidents on the matter, and when half the time to report is gone with no decision the routine checks escalate it to the stand-in, once and on the record (EL-006)

Each person step at the end of the workflow (review, release preparation, recipient approval, delivery) is recorded with who did it and logged like any step; while a run waits for review or once it is approved, anyone who may hold work can put it on hold with reasons, which suspends reliance and stops its release; only someone who may resolve holds can lift it; a restart is refused over a person's hold; reliance resumes only on the unchanged approved report
evidence: step_completed events for person steps; hold_raised and hold_resolved events with reason held_by_person

control: Hard offline: the operating system's kernel refuses every network connection from the program, whatever code asks (Python, native libraries, io_uring, child processes; on Linux a seccomp filter on every thread that cannot be removed until the program exits); anyone signed in can switch it on at once, and starting hard offline every time needs the right to manage the configuration and the passphrase; a server binds its port first and keeps answering; every change is recorded, and the header shows whether the kernel enforces it
evidence: network_mode audit events; the header and Settings, System show what enforces it

control: Live official legal databases (EU: Publications Office CELLAR and EUR-Lex; UK: legislation.gov.uk and Find Case Law) are reached only after their licence is read and a named person approves them, only from their declared hosts over HTTPS, one request at a time through the network guard, and never under hard offline; each authority is stored as a dated source version with what was retrieved, when, its status and repeal history; legislation is judged on the version in force on the matter's relevant date, and each provision relied on on its own status: a section repealed while the rest of the Act stays in force fails from its repeal date, read from the database's own annotation, and a repeal for another part of the kingdom, in part or without a date goes to a person; an amended EU act is read in the consolidated version in force on the date (the act as published before its first), with recitals from the act as published and a note that the Official Journal texts are authentic; redirects stay on the source's host and on HTTPS, and an empty answer is reported, never read as an act without text; a judgment the database records no treatment for goes to a person; an EU judgment's status basis names the later judgments and Advocate General's opinions CELLAR records as citing it, for that person to read
evidence: source_approved audit events; each authority's retrieval time, content hash and status basis in the evidence pack

control: Research and the linking of facts to issues also work by meaning, with an embedding model run on this machine: research fuses the ranking by words with the ranking by meaning (the ranking by words weighted 0.2), and a fact is linked to the issue it is closest to when it stands out for that issue. Meaning decides only which passages are offered and which facts are filed under an issue: every passage is quoted word for word and verified like any other. The model and its file's fingerprint are recorded as the run's retrieval and linking tools, so a change of model is a change between runs; the report says how research was done, and says so when meaning could not run or covered only part of the sources. Beside what a party says of an authority, the report shows the authority's passage closest in meaning, chosen during the run and kept with the finding so the report is rebuilt the same without the model, and labelled as a pointer. The model is never given more text than it was trained on. Vectors of a case's own words (its issues, facts and what a party says) are made when needed and never stored, so nothing derived from a case outlives its purge; only the vectors of the legal sources' passages are kept. A fact filed under an issue by meaning alone is recorded as such and marked in the report for the reviewer to check, since meaning finds more links and some are wrong. Chosen automatically, the model is one measured to link facts at least as precisely as words do, when one is present
evidence: run.tool_versions retrieval and linking; research_by_meaning, research_by_words and research_partial in the report's limits; source_indexed audit events

control: Legal research and fact linking are measured against answers fixed in advance: 70 issues over fifteen EU and UK instruments as their official databases publish them (recall at 5 and 10, MRR, nDCG at 10, and how much of what is offered is in point), and 50 facts in four disputes (precision, recall, F1). The settings of searching and linking by meaning were chosen on half of each benchmark and checked on the other half. Research by words may not fall below its measured figures: the tests fail if it does. Anyone can rerun them (eli-legal evaluate)
evidence: eli-legal evaluate --json output; the figures in docs/5_legal_and_compliance and the release notes

control: The application can be read and used by people who are not technical and by people who find small text hard to read: every page is named in plain words with what it is for; a Start a new case walkthrough, first in the sidebar, shows how a case is built and explains every question of every part, ticking what is done for the open case; a How to use page takes a case from start to finish and explains every word the application uses; resting the pointer on a column heading, field, button or page explains it; Ctrl and + or - (or Ctrl and the mouse wheel) make everything larger or smaller, everywhere, and the size is remembered; requirements say what the organisation still has to record and take the person to it; the team page of a new case says in words who can approve that kind of case and why someone cannot, and an administrator adds people and changes what their accounts may do there; Named reviewers and a run held for want of one say which accounts may approve and why each person cannot; the Review page offers a decision only on a report awaiting review, says in each state what to do next (a returned report: correct it, then Restart to make the corrections), keeps what the reviewer ticked when it refreshes, and shows a report suspended from reliance with how to end it
evidence: the How to use page and glossary as shipped; the desktop and browser applications

control: An approved report stops leaving the matter the moment an authority it relies on is found no longer good law: the routine checks look at every approved report of every open matter, not only the latest run, and record a suspension with its incident in one transaction, once per report, naming who already received it; preparing a release and sending one consult it immediately before acting, by every route, and a refusal is audited; the approval and earlier releases stay in the record; closing the incident does not end it; only a named reviewer who may approve, with identity confirmed again and a written basis, ends it, by confirming the law again for the report (re-checked at that moment) or by naming a later run re-checked and approved after the suspension, which replaces the report (EL-001)
evidence: reliance_blocks.json and incidents.json in the evidence pack; reliance_block_opened / reliance_denied / reliance_block_resolved events

control: A preservation hold (a litigation hold, an order, a claim expected) stops a matter's content being deleted, at closure or when its retention period ends: a hold on the whole matter refuses the deletion before anything changes, and records the refusal; a hold on named documents keeps those documents' originals, records and text while the rest goes; every deletion goes through one path and leaves a receipt of the SHA-256 of each original deleted, what was kept and under which hold, matched by the ledger's record of it; the matter's lead or the compliance owner places a hold with its basis and authority; only the legal or data-protection owner releases it, with identity confirmed again and a reason; the holds outlive the content (EL-004)
evidence: preservation_holds records; disposal receipts (artifacts/disposals/<matter>/); preservation_hold_placed / disposal_refused / content_disposed / retention_purge / preservation_hold_released events

control: Each matter is opened as practice (demonstration, training, testing: no real case material, and every report says it is not for reliance) or real. A real matter's work starts, restarts, is approved and leaves only under a deployment authorisation in force that covers its legal system and kind of matter: proposed by someone who manages compliance with references to the design review, the lawyer's validation of the legal-system packs, the security assessment, the evaluation, the impact assessments and the oversight plan; signed by a provider lead and a different deployer lead; expiring within 400 days; pinned to the software version, policy and model, so a change voids it until approved again; revocable at once. A real matter also needs its legal-system packs validated, and on a court, tribunal or neutral's matter the approving reviewer must not be the person who ran the work. Every refusal names what is missing and is audited (EL-005)
evidence: deployment authorisations (registry); deployment_proposed / deployment_signed / deployment_revoked / deployment_denied events
